name: certified_branch_regret
rule: (2 + weight/max(1e-9,weight+conflict_weight) + 0.01/(1+degree) if weight >= neighbor_cover or weight+residual_pack >= excluded_cover else 0.75*(weight+residual_pack-excluded_pack)/max(1e-9,weight+residual_pack,excluded_pack) + 0.25*(weight+residual_cover-excluded_cover)/max(1e-9,weight+residual_cover,excluded_cover) + 0.1*weight/max(1e-9,weight+neighbor_cover) + 0.02*neighbor_edges/max(1,degree*(degree-1)/2) - 0.001*degree/max(1,remaining_count))
rationale: The identical parents share a backbone of forced-root residual packing and clique-cover estimates, neighborhood opportunity cost, and conflict structure. I turn this into inclusion-versus-exclusion regret: compare completions after selecting the root with completions after only excluding it, emphasizing normalized feasible advantage over optimistic cover advantage. First prioritize roots whose weight covers every independent alternative in their active neighborhood, or whose forced feasible completion reaches the exclusion upper bound. Otherwise use branch regret, with neighborhood replacement efficiency and density providing small structural tie breakers.
